_comment: Source of truth for the announcement bar: the slim strip above the nav on the
marketing pages. scripts/announcements.mjs validates this file and renders the
bar; `npm run announce:render` writes it into the static pages, `npm run build`
does the same, and the blog and channel guide get it from scripts/site-chrome.mjs.
`npm test` fails if a page is out of date with this file.
Each message: id, enabled, text, and optionally link, startsAt, endsAt.
id        a short slug. A visitor who closes a message does not see that id again,
so a new announcement needs a new id.
enabled   false keeps it in the file but off the pages.
text      one plain sentence, 140 characters at most. No dashes used as stops, no emoji.
link      optional. The whole message links there: https://... or a path like /roku.
startsAt  optional, ISO 8601 with an offset, e.g. 2026-11-09T00:00:00-05:00.
endsAt    optional, same format. The browser hides the message after this time,
even on a page deployed before it. Set enabled to false when you next
touch the file so the markup goes too.
The message scrolls left without stopping, repeated with a bullet between, at
about 50 pixels a second. A pause button, hovering and keyboard focus all hold it.
Several enabled messages take turns, one at a time, each after a full pass.
Under reduced motion nothing scrolls or rotates and a long message wraps: the
first live message shows and closing it shows the next.
